title: Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rav Yehudah’s student, citing Chullin 48b in the supplied text (the episode is at [45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.45b.20-21)): Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak wished to go to Bei Chozai; he came before Rav Yehudah and said, “Let the Master show me where the branches [of the spinal cord] divide” — he said to him, “Come, I will teach you.” He is also mentioned in [Megillah 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.10b.30): Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak opened this section with an introduction from here: “For we are slaves.”[^2]

notes.text: The supplied Chullin 48b locator remains in the translation. Named Davidson Chullin 45b instead contains Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak’s Bei Chozai journey and request to locate the spinal-cord branches. It writes Rabbi Yehudah where Hyman writes Rav Yehudah, and replies “bring me a kid”; those witness differences remain distinct from Hyman’s “come, I will teach you.” This resolves the reviewer’s nonlocation without erasing the old locator.

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=916&lang=en) cites Chullin 45b. The linked passage calls the teacher Rabbi Yehudah. He first asks Dimi to bring a kid, then offers to teach him and quotes Shmuel. In Megillah the introduction starts on 10b, and the [Ezra verse follows on 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.11a.1).
